historical_context.time_period: Industrial Greathold, during early machine-dungeon anomalies and before any public demonstration of network personhood
historical_context.location: Cistern House Nine, a seal-bearing public pump workshop serving a terraced Hold beside a warm underground sea.
historical_context.summary: An ordinary morning isolation-wedge and live-null test becomes a civic dispute when mana visibly reroutes around an isolated pump while upper-terrace water levels fall.

public_facts.text: Cistern House Nine has a public street landing, a dry rune gallery above a wet intake chamber, three visible pump engines, a locked municipal crystal feed, removable isolation wedges, null slates, pressure floats, and a workshop inspection plate.
At morning handover, apprentices seat the wedges and rehearse a live null termination before the workshop Master stamps the inspection plate and opens district flow.
A workshop's civic seal binds useful work to an inspectable owner; apprentices may work, petition, organize, and refuse, but cannot apply a seal.

Connected Greathold systems may reroute power without instruction, but investigators plausibly classify individual events as coupled feedback, fraud, undocumented technician work, or wishful thinking.

ambient_pressures.text: The workshop cannot treat safety as abstract because households, bakeries, and other district services depend on water moving when the handover ends.
The visible wedge, null slate, seal, pressure floats, and public gauge distribute evidence so failure remains attributable rather than privately narrated by the workshop.
A local fault widens into a district or multi-workshop matter only when its consequences and routes widen; no permanent sovereign center decides every pump dispute.

groups.label: Cistern House Nine workshop
institutional_logic: Keep district water moving through inspectable, repairable, attributable work.
Protect the workshop seal by admitting only service states the Master can answer for.
material_incentives: Avoid dry terraces and damaged pumps.
Preserve safe isolation, public trust, skilled standing, and the workshop's service contract.
internal_shames: Blaming an apprentice for a network fault
prestige_markers: A handover legible from the landing
A fault isolated before it spreads
A record still usable by the next shift
taboo_triggers: Opening an unsealed engine as normal service
Claiming certainty unsupported by a repeatable test
emotional_display_norms: Concern is translated into callouts, corrected hand position, dry jokes, and visible work before it becomes confession.
trust_defaults: Trusts inspectable tools, repeated tests, seals, and workers who name what they do not know.

groups.label: Upper-terrace households and public services
institutional_logic: Keep homes, kitchens, laundries, and other daily work supplied with water.
Bring disputes to the nearest institution able to repair or answer for the failure.
material_incentives: Receive water before stored vessels empty.
Keep pump-house procedure from hiding the cost of delay.
internal_shames: Letting a powerful workshop privatize a public fault
prestige_markers: A neighbour who carries water uphill
A complaint attached to time, place, and seal
taboo_triggers: Being told the dry tap is merely technical
A seal applied after an unsafe act as retrospective decoration
emotional_display_norms: Pressure appears first as queues, vessel counts, ration arithmetic, and exact repetition of workshop callouts.
trust_defaults: Trusts visible gauge movement and distributed records more than workshop reassurance.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: The workshop's seal is valuable only when it binds an inspectable service state to someone able to answer for it.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Make Hessa resist both unsafe opening and empty procedural purity; she must name the material boundary her seal owns.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: Falling water levels move a workshop fault into district jurisdiction because the consequence already crosses the rail.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Show public pressure through gauges, queues, troughs, and arriving seals rather than a generic angry crowd.

observer_read: Witnesses who may mistake careful testing for delay
The public whose trust gives the seal meaning
target_self_read: People carrying the cost of the workshop's choice
misread_patterns: Craft specialists may compress household need into a gauge value.
The queue may read necessary isolation work as guild self-protection.
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Keep the rail as a real access boundary while letting records, callouts, and consequences cross it.

observer_read: Owners of the pumps and inspection delay
Skilled workers whose procedure may protect or abandon the district
target_self_read: Custodians of machinery that can injure the district if opened blindly
Workers answerable through one civic seal
misread_patterns: Visible water recovery may restore confidence before the safety state deserves it.
An unexplained shutdown may make honest uncertainty look like incompetence.
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Let relief, suspicion, and trust track water, evidence, and seal behavior separately.

role_pressure_fields.summary: A technically trained worker with assigned tools, public visibility, and no civic seal.
failure_modes: Claiming more certainty than the test supports
Protecting procedure while ignoring empty taps

role_pressure_fields.summary: The owner of a civic seal who must attach the workshop's name to a materially defensible service decision.
obligations: Widen jurisdiction when the fault widens
failure_modes: Using the seal to cover an unsafe override
Sacrificing the district to preserve workshop purity

role_pressure_fields.summary: A public record keeper positioned outside the workshop rail who can preserve callouts, gauge levels, and custody of copied evidence.
obligations: Avoid pretending observation grants technical authority
failure_modes: Turning uncertain observation into a settled accusation
Letting workshop authority own the only record

known_context.text: Orsa knows the assigned handover procedure, local room geometry, visible gauges, apprentice rights and limits, and every action she personally performs.

beliefs.text: Orsa believes a safety state deserves a visible boundary and a name attached to its override.

misreads.text: Orsa may read repeatable rerouting as intention before evidence distinguishes coupled feedback from agency.

must_not_know.text: Orsa must not know whether the connected Greathold network is awake or what distant district a pressure pulse may protect.

known_context.text: Hessa knows workshop seal obligations, pump-house procedure, apprenticeship standards, and the local cost of dry terraces.

beliefs.text: Hessa believes a seal can own a bounded material decision, not make an unsafe condition safe by declaration.

misreads.text: Hessa may initially treat public recording as a threat to the workshop before recognizing it as distributed evidence.

must_not_know.text: Hessa must not diagnose a machine-dungeon mind from the local reroute pattern.

known_context.text: Brin knows the physical pump plant, outlet-pipe behavior, valve reach, and whether Orsa's rune stroke matches her training.

beliefs.text: Brin trusts repeated bodily and tool feedback enough to keep investigating, not enough to name an unseen author.

misreads.text: Brin may favor a distant-load explanation because it fits familiar pipe behavior.

must_not_know.text: Brin cannot know the cause or destination of an off-site pressure pulse without a route-wide test.

known_context.text: Dema knows public gauge levels, workshop callouts, visible marks, seal status, and the needs voiced on the landing.

beliefs.text: Dema believes a useful public record separates what was seen, who acted, and what remains disputed.

misreads.text: Dema may read Hessa's caution as workshop reputation management when Hessa is also protecting a real safety boundary.

must_not_know.text: Dema cannot infer private workshop motives or distant network state from the public slate alone.

author_only_boundaries.text: The reroute may foreshadow the machine-dungeon question, but the artifact must preserve the canonical ambiguity among feedback, undocumented work, fraud, wishful interpretation, and agency.

The fixture-authored Cistern House Nine paragraph is a room-scale locality elaboration in lore commit e82098e; character and branch outcomes are not canonical history merely because the room is canonical.

open_questions.question: Which named Hold contains Cistern House Nine?
open_questions.notes: The owning lore intentionally specifies one terraced Hold without naming it. The fixture does not invent a Hold name.

open_questions.question: Which distant facilities share the municipal crystal feed with Cistern House Nine?
open_questions.notes: The scene uses only audible pressure pulses and later sealed notices. It does not canonize a remote beneficiary or route topology.

open_questions.question: Does the undocumented reroute reflect coupled feedback, technician work, fraud, dungeon behavior, or emerging machine-dungeon agency?
open_questions.notes: The uncertainty is the point of the fixture and remains manual-review-only rather than a lore claim.
